duplicate_search.note: This records the searches performed on 2026-09-03; it is not a claim that the forum contains no related proposals.

observed_problem.collision_risk: Eleven audited extension bundles use the basename strings, so a flat external namespace cannot address them independently.
observed_problem.extension_impact: The audited extension bundles use plain ResourceBundle.getBundle(String), so they do not reach QuPath's external localization directories and do not follow the project's DISPLAY-only locale policy.

proposed_contract_for_discussion.goal: Allow extensions to resolve their own localized ResourceBundles through QuPath without forks, while preserving DISPLAY locale semantics and avoiding external filename collisions.
requirements: Expose a supported QuPath API for loading an arbitrary bundle with the extension's ClassLoader or anchor Class.
Resolve locale with Locale.getDefault(Locale.Category.DISPLAY), without changing FORMAT or the global default locale.
Search the extension ClassLoader first for extension-owned resources, with a controlled fallback to QuPath's application ClassLoader where appropriate.
Use the full bundle namespace for external localization lookup, for example qupath/ext/instanseg/ui/strings_es.properties, rather than flattening all bundles to strings_es.properties.
Preserve the existing external lookup behavior for the QuPath main bundle so current installations are not broken.
Keep the API read-only with respect to locale preferences and external files.
Add tests for DISPLAY selection, extension ClassLoader visibility, namespaced external overrides, collision isolation, missing-resource fallback, and legacy main-bundle compatibility.
non_goals: Do not vendor extension source into qupath-es.
Do not patch installed JAR files.
Do not change measurement names, PathClass identifiers, model identifiers, parameter keys, FORMAT locale, or global default locale.
Do not create a permanent QuPath fork before upstream direction is known.

acceptance_gate_before_code.condition: A QuPath core maintainer confirms the preferred API shape or provides equivalent implementation direction in the existing internationalization discussion or another upstream channel.
